summary: A quantity field: formats and parses in the user's locale, clamps to bounds, steps with − and + or the arrow keys, and never changes under the scroll wheel unless asked.
useWhen: the value is a quantity someone might add to or compare — a price, a count, a percentage, a duration
the value has bounds or a step the field should enforce
the value needs formatting — currency, percent, units — in the user's locale

useInstead.when: the value is made of digits but is not a quantity — a phone number, postcode, card number, account or order ID
useInstead.why: a number field strips leading zeros, adds grouping separators and offers + and −, all of which corrupt an identifier. Nobody increments a postcode

useInstead.when: the value is a phone number
a rough value within a range matters more than an exact one — volume, a zoom level
useInstead.why: a stepper that takes forty presses to cross the range is the wrong control; a track shows where the value sits

lg.use: a form where this value is the main input

requires: `label` or `aria-label` — the accessible name. A unit shown by `formatOptions` is not a name
guarantees: Arrow Up and Down step the value from the field; Page Up and Down step by ten; Home and End go to the bounds
the − and + buttons are named and out of the tab order, because the arrow keys already do their job from the field
every size's step buttons are at least 24px square — WCAG 2.5.8
the field is `type="text"` with the matching `inputMode`, so phones show a numeric keyboard without the native number input's parsing quirks
notes: the scroll wheel does not change the value unless `isWheelDisabled={false}` — a focused number input edited by scrolling past it is the classic bug
`onChange` fires on commit — blur, Enter, a step — not per keystroke. `null` means empty; `NaN` never reaches the caller

antiPatterns.why: "02134" becomes 2,134 — leading zero gone, separator added, and a + button nobody should press
the native number input changes under the scroll wheel, cannot show currency or grouping, and reports an empty string for input it cannot parse

antiPatterns.dont: a unit typed into the label and the value — label="Price ($)" with a "$" typed in
antiPatterns.why: formatOptions displays and parses the unit in the user's locale; a hand-typed symbol is text the parser has to reject
this component converts the hook's NaN to null at the boundary, so NaN never arrives
